claims.statement: North Carolina policy administration separates the attached HO 01 32 contract layer, NCDOI-2018-03 fungi-limit disclosure layer, NCDOI-2021-06 claims-administration layer, and internal Rule 550 underwriting layer; Rule 550 is not customer-facing coverage language, and HO 01 32 expressly references only NCDOI-2021-06 B.2 for claim adjustment and consistent deductible application.

The source set dates HO 01 32 to 2018-05-01, NCDOI-2018-03 to 2018-03-12 with prospective application to coverage issued, renewed, amended, or replaced after issuance, and NCDOI-2021-06 to 2021-06-01 with prospective application to subsequent claims-handling conduct.

When attached to the HO-3 policy, HO 01 32 changes only its stated provisions, controls over conflicting policy language for those provisions, leaves unchanged terms applicable, and does not extend coverage beyond its express terms.

HO 01 32 sets a $5,000 maximum for all loss caused by fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria regardless of the number of insureds, claims, damaged properties, or occurrences, while providing no coverage for such loss unless coverage is expressly provided; its definitions include mold, mildew, mycotoxins, and moisture-caused wet rot involving fungi.

The HO 01 32 $5,000 contract term is distinct from the base fungi exclusion, any separately attached HO 04 81 write-back, and NCDOI-2018-03 disclosure; neither a disclosure nor HO 01 32 itself creates fungi coverage that must be expressly provided by the composed policy.

For a policy containing a fungi, wet-rot, or bacteria limitation, NCDOI-2018-03 requires a conspicuous, understandable, accurate, retainable disclosure that identifies the limitation and affected coverage, distinguishes it from other restrictions, and states that the most the insurer will pay is $5,000; the disclosure must not broaden, waive, or contradict the contract.

The fungi disclosure must be delivered before acceptance of new coverage and with applicable coverage information for new business, renewal, replacement coverage, and an endorsement or policy change that adds or changes the limitation; material renewal changes require clear notice, oral disclosure alone is insufficient, and permitted electronic delivery must be accessible and retainable.

The insurer must retain the delivered fungi-disclosure version and delivery evidence, remain responsible when producers, agents, administrators, or systems deliver it, and obtain Department approval before using filed fungi disclosure materials or revisions; superseded materials must be withdrawn.

A fungi allegation or observation alone cannot support denial or limitation; the insurer must investigate the reported facts, determine whether a covered cause produced the condition, distinguish fungi damage from other covered damage, identify the relied-on policy provision, and give a written factual and policy explanation for a partial denial or limitation.

Fungi-related claim files must preserve the policy provisions considered, communications, requested information, investigation and evidence, valuation, and decision basis; the insurer must consider later material information, avoid unrelated requests and unreasonable delay, and keep claims communications consistent with the policy and disclosure without expanding the $5,000 contract limit.

HO 01 32 applies a Windstorm and Hail Deductible of 1% to 5% to covered direct loss caused by windstorm or hail, including when another covered cause contributes; it applies before payment, treats loss from the same general weather conditions as one occurrence, and does not create coverage for excluded or noncovered property.

For an increase in the windstorm deductible, HO 01 32 requires written notice to the named insured at least 30 days before the increase takes effect; the notice must identify the increase and effective date, the increase applies only to a covered loss on or after that date, and a reduction does not require this advance notice.

The HO 01 32 Named Storm Period runs while a governmental Weather Authority watch or warning for a Named Storm affects any part of North Carolina and ends when that watch or warning is withdrawn or expires; causation must be determined from loss facts and reliable evidence, not from a storm occurrence or damage-discovery time alone.

A Named Storm Period does not create coverage or make unrelated damage deductible-subject; when the Named Storm Deductible applies, the insurer reduces covered loss under its terms, and the insured must promptly report the loss, protect and preserve property, permit inspection, retain records, cooperate, and provide available cause evidence.

For covered property in a designated Seacoast Territory, HO 01 32 defines Windstorm to include wind, hail, and wind-driven rain, applies a separate Windstorm Deductible to Windstorm Loss, and caps that deductible at 10% of Coverage A without reducing the limit of liability.

HO 01 32 requires at least 15 days' written notice before cancellation for nonpayment, at least 30 days' written notice before cancellation for another permitted reason with the reason stated, and at least 45 days' written notice before nonrenewal with the coverage-end date stated.

The insured's North Carolina claim duties include prompt notice, mitigation and protective repairs, preservation of damaged property and evidence, inspection access, cooperation, reasonably available records and estimates, signed or sworn proof of loss when requested, examination under oath when reasonably requested, forwarding legal process, truthful information, and preservation of recovery rights.

The insurer must handle claims in good faith with qualified and supervised personnel, acknowledge communications, investigate reasonably before denial or refusal to pay, use relevant reliable information, identify relied-on policy provisions, pay undisputed amounts when due, and give clear written explanations for denials, limitations, reservations, partial payments, or partial denials; delegation does not transfer insurer responsibility.

For an HO 01 32 claim, the insurer must acknowledge receipt within 30 days, accept or reject within 30 business days after receiving requested items needed for the decision, and pay an accepted claim within 30 business days after payment becomes due; an action against the insurer must be brought within three years after the date of loss after policy compliance and subject to applicable law.

North Carolina claim-related notices must ordinarily be written or lawfully electronic, understandable, identify the insurer and contact method, explain relied-on policy provisions and material facts, distinguish accepted and disputed portions, state the basis for the claim position, and preserve recipient, delivery, investigation, evaluation, payment, and decision records; later material information must be considered and undisputed amounts cannot be withheld solely because another portion remains under review.

NCDOI-2021-06 requires written claims-handling procedures and, when the Department requires a filing, disclosure of the insurer's acknowledgment, investigation, evaluation, payment, and written-decision standards; material procedure changes must be filed before use unless directed otherwise, and records must show compliance by delegated personnel.

Rule 550 requires pre-bind delegated-authority review and referral or documentation for North Carolina risks including Coverage A above $700,000, roof age at least 18 years, unresolved ownership or occupancy, business or rental activity, water and moisture conditions, unrepaired losses, fungi-aggregate changes, requests exceeding the seacoast deductible ceiling, incomplete or conflicting material information, and exceptions; these are internal underwriting controls and cannot alter coverage.
